prompt: Compose a complete 64-second instrumental ambient score for a quiet hand-drawn short film called The Path That Draws Itself. A small chalk stick figure draws an amber line through a charcoal forest; the line begins drawing itself, the figure feels relief and then unease at its empty hands, retrieves its pencil, draws a different route and walks onto it. Emotional tone: intimate, thoughtful, melancholy, uncertain, with a small honest return of agency near the end. This accompanies a low, calm male spoken narration, so keep the music sparse and leave plenty of space for words. Instruments: soft dusty analog pads, a few warm muted felt-piano notes with a long delicate reverb tail, a very faint bowed low-string texture. Slow freely breathing phrasing; no obvious beat or rhythmic percussion. A tiny two- or three-note motif, never a busy foreground melody. Minor and suspended harmony, warm but slightly unsettled, without horror or melodrama. First 0-18 seconds: quiet hazy forest atmosphere and isolated piano notes, gently curious. At 18-35 seconds: slightly colder suspended harmonies and a subtle sense of dependence and uncertainty, no loud swell. At 35-43 seconds: make space, then let the little piano motif return as the pencil is picked up. At 43-61 seconds: a warmer, more grounded variation of the same motif as the new route is drawn and followed, still restrained and unresolved rather than triumphant. At 61-64 seconds: a soft natural decay into silence with no abrupt cutoff. Smooth continuous development, no dramatic transitions, no trailer impacts, no drums, no ticking, no risers, no bright cymbals, no big bass, no loud lead instruments. Absolutely no vocals, humming, choir, spoken words or lyrics. Original instrumental underscore, gentle stereo width, soft transients, clean and atmospheric.
